content.content:
1	# Entire - CLI
2	
3	This repo contains the CLI for Entire.
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh
8	
9	## Key Directories
10	
11	### Commands (`cmd/`)
12	
13	- `entire/`: Main CLI entry point. Also home to kubectl-style external-command resolution (`entire <name>` → `entire-<name>` on PATH) — see [External Commands](docs/architecture/external-commands.md).
14	- `entire/cli`: CLI utilities and helpers (Cobra commands, helpers, group roots)
15	- `entire/cli/commands`: actual command implementations
16	- `entire/cli/agent`: agent implementations (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi) - see [Agent Integration Checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) and [Agent Implementation Guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md)
17	- `entire/cli/strategy`: strategy implementation (manual-commit) - see section below
18	- `entire/cli/checkpoint`: checkpoint storage abstractions (ephemeral and persistent)
19	- `entire/cli/session`: session state management
20	- `entire/cli/integration_test`: integration tests (simulated hooks)
21	- `e2e/`: E2E tests with real agent calls (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md))
22	
23	### Command Layout
24	
25	The visible CLI is organized around a set of noun groups plus a small set of
26	top-level verbs. The groups are the canonical home for each verb. Newer
27	experimental command families are discoverable through `entire labs` and
28	their canonical paths are always runnable.
29	
30	Experimental commands are gated by a build-time visibility flag (the
31	`cmd/entire/cli/experimental` package): they are shown — grouped under an
32	"Experimental commands:" help section — in developer and nightly builds, and
33	hidden in stable release builds. Visibility is toggled by `experimental.Visible`
34	(default `"true"`), which GoReleaser stamps `"false"` only on stable tags
35	(`.Prerelease` empty); nightly (`vX.Y.Z-nightly.*`) and local builds leave it at
36	the default. Register a command as experimental with `experimental.Register(parent,
37	child)` instead of `parent.AddCommand(child)`. Gating only controls visibility —
38	the commands are always runnable in every build.
39	
40	- `session` (alias: `sessions`): `list`, `info`, `tokens`, `stop`, `attach`, `adopt`, `resume`, `current`.
41	  `resume` with a branch arg switches to it and resumes its session; with no arg
42	  it opens an interactive picker of stopped sessions (across all worktrees),
43	  resolving each to its branch and pointing at the owning worktree when the
44	  branch is checked out elsewhere. Resume keeps an existing local session log
45	  as-is by default (`--force` overwrites it from the checkpoint).
46	  `adopt` moves an active session from another repo or worktree into the current
47	  worktree and resets target-local checkpoint bookkeeping so future commits link
48	  to the adopted session from the new location.
49	- `checkpoint` (aliases: `cp`, `checkpoints`): `list`, `explain`, `tokens`, `search`.
50	  `explain` also takes `--repo <owner/name>`, the drill-down for a cross-repo
51	  `search` hit: it reads the checkpoint from that repo's entire-api cell over
52	  HTTP (`/repos/{repo_id}/checkpoints/{id}` plus `.../transcript/raw`) rather
53	  than fetching git objects, so a foreign checkpoint never enters this repo's
54	  object store, ref namespace, or `tokens profile`. It needs a full checkpoint
55	  ID and a pushed checkpoint; `--commit`, `--session`, `--search-all`, and
56	  `--generate` are rejected with it, and naming the current repo is a no-op
57	  that falls through to the local path. See `checkpoint_api_reader.go`
58	  (`apiCheckpointReader`, which implements the two checkpoint reader tiers and
59	  deliberately not `Writer`) and `explain_repo.go`.
60	- `agent`: bare opens the interactive agent selector, plus `list`, `add`, `remove`
61	- `configure`: bare prints help and a hint pointing at `entire agent`; flags
62	  manage non-agent settings (telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy
63	  options, summary provider). Agent CRUD lives under `entire agent`.
64	- `auth`: `login`, `logout`, `status`, `contexts`, `use`, plus
65	  `token` (prints the active control-plane bearer to stdout for scripting/curl;
66	  honors `ENTIRE_TOKEN`, else the refreshed active-context login JWT). `token`
67	  also takes `--jurisdiction <slug>` (e.g. `us`, `eu`), which instead mints a
68	  jurisdictional identity token (RFC 8693 exchange, `scope=openid`,
69	  `aud=<jurisdiction host>`) for that jurisdiction's entire-api cells (e.g.
70	  `https://aws-us-east-2.api.entire.io/api/v1`), which reject the control-plane
71	  bearer; it exchanges `ENTIRE_TOKEN` when set (deriving the environment from the
72	  env token's `aud`), else the active login. `auth status` shows the caller's
73	  home jurisdiction so the slug is discoverable. `logout`
74	  takes `--everywhere` (revoke every session on the active core, not just the
75	  current one) and `--all-contexts` (log out of every saved login)
76	- `doctor`: bare runs the scan-and-fix flow, plus `trace`, `logs`, `bundle`
77	- `org`: control-plane organization management — `create`, `list`, `get`, `delete`
78	- `project`: control-plane project management — `create`, `list`, `get`, `delete`
79	- `repo`: control-plane repository lifecycle — `create`, `list`, `get`, `delete`,
80	  `clone`, plus the `mirror` and `visibility` subtrees. Git content operations
81	  (log, diff, …) are intentionally out of scope. The `mirror` subtree is
82	  server-side (`create`, `list`, `get`, `remove`, `collaborators`) with one
83	  exception: `mirror use` repoints the *current clone's* git remote at a mirror
84	  (local git config only — it creates nothing server-side). Interactively it
85	  picks among the repo's placements and asks whether to replace the remote
86	  (preserving the old URL under `--upstream`) or add a separate one;
87	  non-interactively it repoints `--remote` directly. Both `use` and `clone`
88	  choose a placement through the shared `selectPlacement` picker. `clone`
89	  accepts a native `/et/<project>/<repo>` ref, a mirror `/gh/<owner>/<repo>`
90	  ref, or a full `entire://` URL passed through verbatim. **Every ref names its
91	  forge**: the leading token alone decides which grammar is tried, and the bare
92	  `<project>/<repo>` shorthand was removed because both forges take that shape
93	  and nothing in it says which was meant (#2252).
94	  Requiring the prefix is a **namesquatting** guard, not tidiness: without it,
95	  whichever namespace the CLI defaulted to could shadow the other, and
96	  `TestCloneRefAlwaysRequiresItsForgePrefix` pins that no forge-less pair
97	  resolves in either parser or in the command. It holds only for *intent* —
98	  lookups are already unambiguous because native rows are stored prefixed in the
99	  same `full_name` index (`et/<project>/<repo>`), which is why the bare-pair
100	  `--repo` filters on `search`/`experts`/`explain` cannot cross namespaces
101	  either.
102	  Native names are validated client-side against the server's own rules
103	  (`nativeProjectRe`/`nativeRepoRe`, mirroring `normalizeName` in entiredb
104	  `core/resource/project_name.go`); those bounds are server parity only and buy
105	  a local error instead of a control-plane round trip, so a failure is phrased
106	  as what the server accepts rather than as a rule of ours — drift is
107	  one-directional and only a *looser* server would make us wrong. A ref matching
108	  no grammar gets a targeted error (`invalidCloneRefError`) in descending
109	  confidence: a ref naming `github.com` is pointed at its `/gh/` form, a ref
110	  that declared a forge token keeps its own parser's reason, a bare pair is
111	  offered the forge-qualified readings that would actually parse
112	  (`bareRefSuggestions`), and anything left lists the accepted shapes.
113	  A native ref resolves project → repo ULID → `GetRepo`, whose response is the
114	  only one carrying both `clusterHost` and `path`, and clones
115	  `entire://<clusterHost><path>` from the repo's home cluster (`--cluster` is
116	  rejected on native refs).
117	  A trailing `.git` is never part of a repo name, on **either** backend
118	  (`gitDirSuffix` documents the mechanics): every ref parser drops it and `repo
119	  create` refuses a name ending in it. This is a deliberate client-side
120	  narrowing — GitHub rejects such a name outright, but the server accepts a
121	  native `foo.git` (interior dot, same rule that makes `entire-trails.el` legal)
122	  and strips the suffix for `/gh/` paths only. `gitremote.splitOwnerRepo` trims
123	  unconditionally when reading a remote back, so such a repo is unaddressable by
124	  name once cloned regardless; dropping it everywhere makes the CLI agree with
125	  itself instead of leaving `repo clone` the one path that keeps it. Escape
126	  hatches: the repo's ULID, or a full `entire://` URL. Two consequences worth
127	  knowing — a `foo.git` created through the API or web UI *aliases* onto `foo`
128	  in `resolveRepoRef`, and the durable fix is a server-side rule in
129	  `normalizeName`, not this check.
130	- `grant`: manage access grants and org membership — `org`, `project`, and `repo`
131	  each support `add` / `list` / `remove`
132	
133	Forge tokens (`gh`, `et`) are the path segments of an `entire://` URL, and
134	`gitremote.pathForges` owns the *set* — `IsForgePathToken` answers "is this a
135	forge token", `ForgePathLabels` gives the placeholder spelling of the segments
136	after it (`<owner>/<repo>` vs `<project>/<repo>`) so messages read correctly for
137	both. The token strings are still spelled in a dozen call sites; only the set
138	lives in one place. It is deliberately **not** `hostToForge`, which maps an
139	*upstream* git host to its id: a native repo has no upstream host, so `et` is
140	absent there, and conflating the two made `entire://et/<project>/<repo>` dial a
141	cluster named `et` while `entire://gh/...` got an actionable message.
142	`CanonicalHost` still reads `forgeToHost`, so a native remote falls back to its
143	cluster host rather than inventing a forge host. The legacy `/git/` prefix is
144	excluded because `repo clone` cannot act on such a ref.
145	
146	**Being a forge token says nothing about which APIs accept it** — the name says
147	syntax on purpose. Trails are the current example: entire-api takes `et` in the
148	path but cannot resolve it, so `entire trail` refuses it locally with the real
149	reason (`errTrailsNativeUnsupported`). That refusal has to cover *both* ways a
150	forge reaches the API — named in `--repo` and inferred from the origin remote —
151	and the inferred one is the common path.
152	
153	Experimental commands (gated by the build-time visibility flag above — visible
154	and grouped under "Experimental commands:" in developer/nightly builds, hidden
155	in stable releases, always runnable): `tokens`, `import`, `review`,
156	`investigate`, `blame`, `why`, `experts`, `runner`, and `checkpoint policy`.
157	`tokens` is also advertised through `entire labs`.
158	
159	Top-level lifecycle and standalone commands: `enable`, `disable`, `status`,
160	`login`, `logout`, `clean`, `version`, `dispatch`, `activity`, `help`,
161	`configure`, `agent-help`, `api`, `search`. `search` is the canonical
162	spelling (visible in every build, grouped with Sessions & Checkpoints);
163	`checkpoint search` stays a working alias of the same command.
164	
165	`api` is an authenticated passthrough to Entire's HTTP APIs (gh-style): it
166	attaches the right bearer and dials the right host so callers don't plumb auth
167	themselves. `--to core` (default) hits the control plane; `--to cell` hits an
168	entire-api cell. `--jurisdiction <slug>` (e.g. `us`, `eu`) targets a specific
169	jurisdiction's cell instead of the caller's home cell and implies `--to cell`
170	(cell routing + identity-token exchange live in `auth.NewEntireAPICellClient`
171	via `auth.CellTarget`). `{owner}`/`{repo}`/`{repo_id}` in the path are filled
172	from the current repo's origin remote. It is an escape hatch, so it is absent
173	from `agent-help`'s curated listing but stays in `entire help` and agent-help's
174	footer — an agent that needs raw access must find it rather than hand-roll curl
175	with a token.
176	
177	`agent-help` renders machine-readable, agent-facing usage live from the Cobra
178	command tree (so it always matches the installed binary): bare prints a curated
179	"when to use entire" map; `agent-help <command>` drills into one command's
180	current flags; `--json` emits structured output. It is the single source of
181	truth the first-turn context injection and the `--agent-help-skill` skill point
182	agents at, instead of enumerating a surface that goes stale.
183	
184	#### Where agent-facing text goes
185	
186	| What you have | Where it goes |
187	| --- | --- |
188	| A new command | `agentHelpClassification` in `agent_help_cmd.go` — one entry, keyed by command path, carrying `audience` and `listed` |
189	| "When to use this at all" advice for agents | `agentHelpGuidance` — **never** cobra `Short`/`Long` |
190	| A fact humans need too (e.g. "this output is not stable") | cobra `Long`. Human help is a reference, not a lecture: whoever typed `--help` already chose the command |
191	| A per-task command recommendation | `agent-help`, which is pulled on demand. **Never** the first-turn injection, which carries only invariants true on every turn |
192	
193	**Flag it; don't decide it.** Whether a command is `listed`, and whether it is
194	read-only / task-driven / user-owned, are product judgment calls — they change
195	what agents do unprompted in every user's repo. Take the safe default
196	(unlisted, user-owned), then say in the PR what you picked and why so a human
197	can move it. Never quietly promote a command into the listing or into
198	read-only.
199	
200	CI enforces the mechanical parts, so trust these rather than re-deriving them:
201	every advertised top-level command and every child of a listed group is
202	classified; a read-only group contains no writing subcommand; guidance text
203	never appears in a command's `Short`/`Long`.
204	
205	Hidden commands opt into being advertised here by setting
206	`Annotations[agentHelpAnnotation] = "true"` (e.g. `trail`). Because `agent-help`
207	renders live and lists non-hidden commands, the experimental commands appear in
208	`agent-help` in developer/nightly builds and are absent in stable releases — the
209	advertised surface is build-dependent, matching what `entire help` shows.
210	No-channel agents (Cursor, Copilot CLI, Factory Droid, MCP hosts — no
211	context-injection channel and no agent-help skill template) reach it without an
212	active push. All of them can discover it passively: it is visible in `entire
213	help`, the `entire status` footer points at it, and `entire status --json`
214	exposes it as the `agent_help` field. On top of that, Factory AI Droid (which is
215	banner-only) gets the pointer appended to its SessionStart hook banner, and
216	MCP-host agents can launch the hidden `entire mcp` stdio server, which exposes
217	`agent_help` and `entire_status` as MCP tools using the same live rendering.
218	Enabling a no-channel agent with `--agent-help-skill` reports the skill
219	unsupported and points the agent at this passive path instead.
220	
221	Cobra-native aliases (no hint): `sessions` → `session`, `cp`/`checkpoints` →
222	`checkpoint`.
223	
224	Hidden infrastructure commands: `hooks`, `trail`,
225	`curl-bash-post-install`, `__send_analytics`, `__sweep_sessions`, `mcp` (MCP
226	stdio server for MCP-host agents).
227	
228	Diagnostic subcommands live alongside `doctor.go` as `doctor_logs.go` and
229	`doctor_bundle.go`. Group roots and noun-group children live in files
230	named `<noun>_group.go` and `<noun>_<verb>.go` respectively.

312	### Test Parallelization
313	
314	**Always use `t.Parallel()` in tests.** Every top-level test function and subtest should call `t.Parallel()` unless it modifies process-global state (e.g., `os.Chdir()`).
315	
316	```go
317	func TestFeature_Foo(t *testing.T) {
318	    t.Parallel()
319	    // ...
320	}
321	
322	// Integration tests with TestEnv
323	func TestFeature_Bar(t *testing.T) {
324	    t.Parallel()
325	    env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
326	    // ...
327	}
328	```
329	
330	**Exception:** Tests that modify process-global state cannot be parallelized. This includes `os.Chdir()`/`t.Chdir()` and `os.Setenv()`/`t.Setenv()` — Go's test framework will panic if these are used after `t.Parallel()`.
331	
332	### Git in Tests
333	
334	**Tests that touch git state must use an isolated temp repo — never the real repo CWD.**
335	
336	Many handlers (lifecycle, strategy, hooks) resolve the git repo from CWD via `OpenRepository`, `GetGitCommonDir`, `DetectFileChanges`, etc. Without isolation, tests can create session state files, shadow branches, or other artifacts in the real `.git/` directory.
337	
338	Use the `testutil` helpers:
339	
340	```go
341	tmpDir := t.TempDir()
342	testutil.InitRepo(t, tmpDir)                    // git init + user config + disable GPG
343	testutil.WriteFile(t, tmpDir, "f.txt", "init")  // create a file
344	testutil.GitAdd(t, tmpDir, "f.txt")             // stage it
345	testutil.GitCommit(t, tmpDir, "init")           // commit (needs at least one commit for HEAD)
346	t.Chdir(tmpDir)                                 // redirect CWD-based git resolution
347	```
348	
349	`testutil.InitRepo` configures `user.name`, `user.email`, and disables GPG signing — safe for CI environments without global git config.
350	
351	**Prefer `testutil.InitRepo()` over direct `git.PlainInit()` in tests.** When a test in this repo needs an initialized repository, use `testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)` unless the test specifically needs lower-level initialization behavior that the helper cannot provide. Do not call `git.PlainInit()` directly and then create commits or run CLI git operations without also reproducing the helper's repo-local config.
352	
353	**Do NOT** shell out to `git init`/`git commit` directly without setting user config and `--no-gpg-sign`, and **do NOT** run lifecycle/strategy handlers from the real repo CWD in tests.
354	
355	### Config/Cache/Keyring Isolation in Tests
356	
357	Tests must never read or write the developer's real `~/.config/entire`
358	(contexts.json, version_check.json), `~/.cache/entire` (nodes.json,
359	cluster_cores.json, api_discovery.json), or OS keychain. The developer may be
360	using `entire` for real while tests run.
361	
362	- **Single resolver**: `internal/entireclient/userdirs` is the only place
363	  that resolves the per-user config dir (`userdirs.Config()`:
364	  `$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR` else `~/.config/entire`) and cache dir
365	  (`userdirs.Cache()`: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/entire` else `~/.cache/entire`).
366	  Never derive these paths anywhere else.
367	- **In-process safety net**: `userdirs` and the `tokenstore` default backend
368	  detect `go test` (via `internal/testdirs`) and fall back to a throwaway
369	  per-process temp directory when their env override is unset. The fallback
370	  is shared across tests in one process — for per-test isolation still set
371	  `t.Setenv("ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR", t.TempDir())` and
372	  `tokenstore.UseFileBackendForTesting(...)`.
373	- **Spawned binaries are NOT covered**: `testing.Testing()` is false in a
374	  subprocess. The integration and e2e TestMains set `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`,
375	  `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file`, `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH`, and
376	  `ENTIRE_TEST_AUTH_STORE_FILE` process-wide so every spawned `entire` (and
377	  every agent-invoked hook) inherits isolation. Any new harness that spawns
378	  the real binary must do the same.
379	- **Legacy auth store**: `auth.NewStore()` talks straight to the zalando
380	  keyring; packages whose tests can reach it need `keyring.MockInit()` in
381	  `TestMain` (see `cmd/entire/cli/global_test.go`) — the `testdirs` fallback
382	  does not cover it in-process.
383	
384	### Spawning subprocesses in tests (TTY detection)
385	
386	Tests that spawn the real `entire` or `git` binary need the child to be non-interactive so prompts don't hang on a developer terminal.
387	
388	`interactive.CanPromptInteractively()` resolves in this order:
389	
390	1. `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1` → force interactive ON (any other non-empty value → force OFF).
391	2. `testing.Testing()` → false. In-process `go test` runs are non-interactive by default; no per-test `t.Setenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY", "0")` is needed.
392	3. Agent sentinels (`GEMINI_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `PI_CODING_AGENT`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`) → false.
393	4. `CI=<non-empty-non-false>` → false.
394	5. `/dev/tty` probe, plus its terminal mode → a terminal held in raw mode
395	   (canonical input off) belongs to a full-screen TUI that spawned us, not to a
396	   shell we can prompt: TUI git clients (lazygit, gitui, tig) run `git commit`
397	   as a child while owning the screen, so the hook inherits a `/dev/tty` it
398	   must not prompt on. Fails open when the mode can't be read. See
399	   `interactive/rawmode_unix.go` for the rationale.
400	
401	For subprocesses spawning the real `entire` binary (e2e, integration tests, `entire` calling itself from a hook), prefer `execx.NonInteractive` over env-var plumbing:
402	
403	```go
404	import "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/execx"
405	
406	cmd := execx.NonInteractive(ctx, getTestBinary(), "status")
407	cmd.Dir = repoDir
408	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
409	```
410	
411	`execx.NonInteractive` puts the child in a new session with no controlling terminal (`Setsid` on Unix, `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` on Windows), so the child's `/dev/tty` probe fails naturally. No env var required.
412	
413	`interactive.UnderTest()` returns true when `testing.Testing()` or `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY` is set — use it where code needs to skip a real-terminal operation even if `CanPromptInteractively()` returns true (e.g., reading from `/dev/tty` directly inside `askConfirmTTY`).

477	## Code Patterns
478	
479	### Error Handling
480	
481	The CLI uses a specific pattern for error output to avoid duplication between Cobra and main.go.
482	
483	**How it works:**
484	
485	- `root.go` sets `SilenceErrors: true` globally - Cobra never prints errors
486	- `main.go` prints errors to stderr, unless the error is a `SilentError`
487	- Commands return `NewSilentError(err)` when they've already printed a custom message
488	
489	**When to use `SilentError`:**
490	Use `NewSilentError()` when you want to print a custom, user-friendly error message instead of the raw error:
491	
492	```go
493	// In a command's RunE function:
494	if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(); err != nil {
495	    cmd.SilenceUsage = true  // Don't show usage for prerequisite errors
496	    fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Not a git repository. Please run 'entire enable' from within a git repository.")
497	    return NewSilentError(errors.New("not a git repository"))
498	}
499	```
500	
501	**When NOT to use `SilentError`:**
502	For normal errors where the default error message is sufficient, return the error directly. main.go will print it:
503	
504	```go
505	// Normal error - main.go will print "unknown strategy: foo"
506	return fmt.Errorf("unknown strategy: %s", name)
507	```
508	
509	**Key files:**
510	
511	- `errors.go` - Defines `SilentError` type and `NewSilentError()` constructor
512	- `root.go` - Sets `SilenceErrors: true` on root command
513	- `main.go` - Checks for `SilentError` before printing
514	
515	### `.entire` Must Be a Directory
516	
517	`<worktree-root>/.entire` is either absent or a real directory. A regular file, a
518	symlink — **including a symlink pointing at a perfectly good directory** — a
519	FIFO, a socket, or a device is a broken repo, and a command that would read or
520	write through the path stops instead.
521	
522	**The entries directly inside it must be regular files or directories.** That is
523	an allowlist, not a list of known-bad types: Entire only ever creates files and
524	directories under `.entire`, so anything else arrived some other way and a mode
525	bit nobody has considered yet is refused by default. A symlinked
526	`.entire/metadata` redirects transcripts; a symlinked `.entire/settings.local.json`
527	redirects the file that names the command Entire executes at pre-push; a FIFO in
528	either place hangs the read instead. The scan is one level deep, and
529	`fs.ModeIrregular` is its one deliberate exception — see the entry-scan
530	mechanics below.
531	
532	`paths.ValidateEntireDirAt(worktreeRoot)` / `paths.RequireEntireDir(ctx)`
533	(`paths/entiredir.go`) are the only implementation. The stat is `Lstat`, not
534	`Stat`, which is the whole point: `.entire` holds session metadata, transcripts,
535	and the redaction settings that decide what may be committed, so a path someone
536	else owns the far end of is not one we write through. Absent is fine (Entire is
537	not enabled yet, or `enable` is about to create it). A stat error other than
538	"not exist" is a failure — it is not evidence the invariant is violated, but it
539	is not evidence it holds either, and the caller's next move is to write there.
540	Not memoized, deliberately: the `Lstat` and the one-level listing are free next
541	to the `git rev-parse` that precedes them, and a cached "it was fine" is stale in
542	a long-lived `entire mcp`.
543	
544	**Four failure conditions, each identified positively.** `ErrEntireDirNotDirectory`
545	(the path exists and is the wrong type), `ErrEntireDirUnsupportedEntry` (an entry
546	directly inside it is neither a regular file nor a directory), `ErrEntireDirUnreadable` (`Lstat` or the
547	directory listing failed, so nothing is known about the path), and
548	`ErrRepositoryUnresolved` (the worktree root would not resolve, so there is no
549	path to inspect yet). Callers print a remedy, and the remedies are different
550	things: replace the path, replace the entry, fix ownership/permissions, fix git.
551	Match them with `errors.Is` and give an unmatched error **no** remedy — an `else`
552	branch is how a filesystem `EACCES` came to be answered with advice about
553	`safe.directory`, printed directly under a line that already said "permission
554	denied". `writeEntireDirRemedy` and `writeEntireDirDiagnosis` (doctor's
555	labelled variant: BROKEN / UNREADABLE / UNVERIFIED) both take the error as a
556	parameter so every branch is reachable in a test; staging a genuinely
557	unreadable `.entire` is impractical, since removing execute permission on the
558	repo root breaks worktree-root discovery first and exercises the wrong branch.
559	An unsupported entry and a wrong-typed `.entire` share doctor's BROKEN heading:
560	to the reader they are one condition — something replaced a path Entire owns —
561	differing only in which path and what to put back.
562	
563	**`ErrEntireDirNotDirectory` is not reused for an unsupported entry**, even though
564	both remedies are "replace it". `.entire/settings.json` is not required to be a
565	directory, so telling someone it is not one names the wrong problem. The entry
566	remedy says "replace it with a real file or directory"; the `.entire` remedy says
567	"replace it with a real directory", and `TestEntireDirRemedyMatchesTheCondition`
568	asserts neither branch prints the other's phrase.
569	
570	**Entry-scan mechanics.** `validateEntireDirEntries` does one `os.ReadDir` and
571	passes each `DirEntry.Type()` to `unsupportedEntryType`, with **no `Lstat` of its
572	own** — the type comes from the directory read where the platform reports one,
573	and where it does not, `os.ReadDir` does the `Lstat` internally, *skipping an
574	entry that vanished between the read and the stat*. `DirEntry.Type()` is
575	therefore never unresolved, and `Type() == 0` means a regular file, not unknown
576	(`direntType` returns `^FileMode(0)` for unknown, which sets every bit including
577	`ModeSymlink`, so even a leak would fail closed). Adding an `Lstat` here
578	reintroduces that race, which matters because `.entire/tmp` and
579	`.entire/metadata/<session>` churn under concurrent hooks. The entries are
580	checked **before** `ReadDir`'s error, because `os.ReadDir` returns what it
581	managed to read alongside a partial-read error and an unsupported entry among
582	those is a positive finding — a stronger statement than "the listing failed". One
583	error names the first offender in `ReadDir`'s sorted order (so the message is
584	deterministic) and counts the rest, rather than one error per entry: the remedy
585	is identical for all of them, and a user who reruns the command once per planted
586	entry is paying for our formatting.
587	
588	**`fs.ModeIrregular` is tolerated, and that is the one place the allowlist
589	bends.** Windows overloads the bit: Go maps every reparse tag it has no category
590	for onto it (the `default` arm of `fileStat.mode` in `os/types_windows.go`),
591	which lands NTFS directory junctions *and* OneDrive Files On-Demand placeholders
592	in the same bucket, indistinguishable from a `DirEntry`. Refusing the bucket
593	would hard-fail every command in a repo inside a synced folder, with a remedy the
594	user cannot act on, and the placeholder arrives with nobody attacking anything.
595	The junction it would also catch cannot arrive by checkout — git has no
596	tree-object mode for one — so planting it already requires local code execution,
597	at which point this check is not what stands in the way. **The bit is masked
598	out of the type, not matched against it** — `mode.Type() &^ fs.ModeIrregular`
599	must equal `0` or `fs.ModeDir` — because Windows does not hand it over alone:
600	`ModeDir` is withheld only for a *name-surrogate* reparse tag, and the cloud
601	tags are not surrogates, so a placeholder **directory** arrives as
602	`ModeDir|ModeIrregular` while a junction (a surrogate) arrives as
603	`ModeIrregular` by itself. `.entire`'s own entries are mostly directories, so an
604	exact match on the bare bit would reject `metadata`, `logs`, and `tmp` in exactly
605	the synced folder the tolerance exists for. Masking does not soften the rest of
606	the field: anything carrying a rejected type is rejected whatever else it
607	carries, `ModeIrregular` included.
608	
609	**The comparison is against the whole type field, never `IsRegular`/`IsDir`.**
610	Those examine single bits (`IsDir` is `mode&ModeDir != 0`), so an allowlist
611	keyed on them lets a rejected type in by *also* setting an accepted bit:
612	`ModeDir|ModeSymlink` and `ModeDir|ModeNamedPipe` both satisfy `IsDir`, and so
613	does the all-bits-set unknown mode above — which is what made the "even a leak
614	would fail closed" claim false until it was fixed. An allowlist a rejected type
615	can enter by setting an extra bit is not an allowlist.
616	`TestUnsupportedEntryType` pins each combination. Distinguishing junction from
617	placeholder would mean reading the reparse tag through a
618	Windows-only syscall (`FindFirstFile`, then `Reserved0 & 0x20000000` for the
619	name-surrogate tags); that is the upgrade path if junctions ever become worth
620	catching.
621	
622	**A settings file is never read through a link, and the settings reader enforces
623	that itself.** `readConfined` (`settings/settings.go`) — the chokepoint every
624	settings read funnels through, including `LoadFromFile`, `LoadProjectRaw`,
625	`LoadLocalRaw`, and clone preferences — `Lstat`s the entry through its own
626	`os.Root` handle and refuses a symlink outright, wrapping
627	`paths.ErrEntireDirUnsupportedEntry` via the shared `paths.SymlinkedEntryError`
628	(the symlink-specific message builder, which names the link target; the entry
629	scan reaches it through `unsupportedEntryError` and describes other types with
630	`describeMode`).
631	
632	This is deliberately redundant with the `.entire` entry scan, because the two
633	cover different callers: the scan hangs off the root pre-run and
634	`LoadEntireSettings`, while **eighteen files call `settings.Load` directly** —
635	`strategy/hooks.go`, `manual_commit_hooks.go`, `checkpoint/remote/*`, `review/*`,
636	`investigate/*` — and reach settings without ever passing the pre-run.
637	
638	**`os.Root` confinement is not the invariant, and was not sufficient.** Measured
639	against `readConfined` before the change: an absolute target (even one pointing
640	inside `.entire`) and an escaping relative target were refused, but as `path
641	escapes from parent`, naming neither cause nor fix; and two shapes got through:
642	
643	| link | before | after |
644	| --- | --- | --- |
645	| `settings.local.json -> planted.json` (relative, stays inside) | **followed** | refused |
646	| `settings.json -> missing.json` (dangling) | **ENOENT → silently default settings** | refused |
647	
648	The dangling case was the worse of the two: every caller reads ENOENT as
649	"absent", so a planted link made Entire ignore the project's settings without
650	saying anything. Do not "simplify" the `Lstat` away on the grounds that
651	`os.OpenRoot` already confines the read — it confines it, which is a different
652	property from refusing a link.
653	
654	Writes are already safe and need no equivalent: `jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic`
655	finishes with `os.Rename` over the target, which *replaces* a symlink rather
656	than writing through it.
657	
658	**Non-goals, deliberately.** The scan is *not* recursive — walking deeper would
659	traverse every session's transcripts on every command, and the checkpoint writer
660	already skips symlinks as it walks the metadata directory. It does *not* look at
661	permissions or ownership, only at type. Relocating `.entire/logs` and
662	`.entire/tmp` out of the worktree is a separate change; until then, redirecting
663	them with a symlink is refused rather than supported, and the remedy text says
664	so.
665	
666	Cost of the second phase: measured 8.2µs against 1.0µs for the `Lstat` alone, on
667	a `.entire` holding six subdirectories, three files, and 51 session directories
668	it does not descend into. That is ~0.1% of the `git rev-parse` subprocess that
669	`WorktreeRoot` runs immediately before it, which is why the deliberate
670	non-memoization below still holds.
671	
672	**Guarded is the default.** The root `PersistentPreRunE` runs the check for every
673	command, above both `settings.IsSetUpAny` and `ensureLogger` because each of
674	those already touches the path. A command opts out with
675	`exemptFromEntireDirCheck(cmd)` (`entiredir_guard.go`), which sets an annotation
676	that `skipsEntireDirCheck` inherits down the parent chain, so annotating a group
677	root covers its children. Exemption is registered at the `AddCommand` call in
678	`root.go`, so the whole set reads as one list.
679	
680	Exempt means "this command needs nothing under `.entire`" — control-plane and
681	account commands, `version`/`labs`/`completion`, and `doctor`. It does **not**
682	mean "write through it anyway": `checkEntireDirBeforeRun` returns
683	`safe == false` for an exempt command in a broken repo, which is what keeps
684	`ensureLogger` from creating `.entire/logs` through the symlink. `newLogger`
685	repeats the check for the callers that build a logger outside the pre-run.
686	
687	The pre-run is not the only enforcement point. `LoadEntireSettings` repeats the
688	check, because the pre-run does not cover everything: external plugins are
689	dispatched from `main.go` before cobra runs at all, and exempt commands still
690	reach settings through the post-run telemetry path. Settings are read *from* the
691	directory in question, so loading them is the one operation those callers have
692	in common — the duplicated `Lstat` on the ordinary path buys the guarantee that
693	the check happens at least once on the unusual ones.
694	
695	Outside a git repository there is no worktree root and so nothing to validate,
696	and the check is skipped rather than failing. Commands that need a repository
697	report its absence themselves, with a message about the repository rather than
698	about `.entire`.
699	
700	**That skip requires git's positive verdict, not merely a failed lookup.**
701	`WorktreeRoot` classifies its own failure and wraps `paths.ErrNotARepository`
702	only when git ran, exited non-zero, and said "not a git repository"; exit code
703	128 alone is not the signal, since git also uses it for dubious ownership and
704	permission failures, both of which happen *inside* a repository. Locale
705	variables are pinned to C for that subprocess so the message is recognisable on
706	a translated machine. Every other outcome — git missing from `PATH`, a cancelled
707	context, a killed child, success with empty output — fails closed.
708	
709	The reason is that "we could not find out" is not the same as "there is nothing
710	here", and guessing costs more than a skipped check: `settingsAbsPaths` falls
711	back to a path relative to the *current directory* when the root will not
712	resolve, so a wrong guess reads `./.entire/settings.json` — through the very
713	symlink the guard exists to reject. Refusing to run on a machine whose git is
714	broken is the cheaper mistake. Do not "simplify" `RequireEntireDir` back to
715	treating any `WorktreeRoot` error as absence.
716	
717	Every exemption needs an entry in `entireDirCheckExemptions`
718	(`entiredir_guard_test.go`) giving the reason; `TestEntireDirCheckExemptions`
719	fails both on an unlisted exemption and on a stale entry, so an exemption added
720	to silence a failing test does not pass for a considered one. `help` and
721	`agent-help` are deliberately guarded — someone asking what they can do in this
722	repo is told the repo is broken rather than handed a working command list.
723	`entire <command> --help` is unaffected in every case, because cobra returns
724	`flag.ErrHelp` before it runs any `PersistentPreRunE`; that and `doctor` are the
725	escape hatches.
726	
727	`doctor` is exempt so that it can run **on** a broken repo, which is only worth
728	doing if it says what is wrong: `reportBrokenEntireDir` runs in the doctor
729	group's `PersistentPreRunE` — ahead of doctor's own `PreRunE`, which loads
730	redaction settings from `.entire/settings.json`, and ahead of `doctor logs` /
731	`doctor bundle`, which read `.entire/logs` — prints the diagnosis, and stops. It
732	does not auto-fix: what occupies the path may be someone's data.
733	
734	### Settings
735	
736	All settings access should go through the `settings` package (`cmd/entire/cli/settings/`).
737	
738	**Why a separate package:**
739	The `settings` package exists to avoid import cycles. The `cli` package imports `strategy`, so `strategy` cannot import `cli`. The `settings` package provides shared settings loading that both can use.
740	
741	**Usage:**
742	
743	```go
744	import "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings"
745	
746	// Load full settings object
747	s, err := settings.Load()
748	if err != nil {
749	    // handle error
750	}
751	if s.Enabled {
752	    // ...
753	}
754	
755	// Or use convenience functions
756	if settings.IsSummarizeEnabled() {
757	    // ...
758	}
759	```
760	
761	**Do NOT:**
762	
763	- Read `.entire/settings.json` or `.entire/settings.local.json` directly with `os.ReadFile`
764	- Duplicate settings parsing logic in other packages
765	- Create new settings helpers without adding them to the `settings` package
766	
767	**Key files:**
768	
769	- `settings/settings.go` - `EntireSettings` struct, `Load()`, and helper methods
770	- `config.go` - Higher-level config functions that use settings (for `cli` package consumers)
771
